utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Glad to see that the accused are fit and well and here. And it's unfortunate that the transport delayed our start. Good afternoon, sir. If I could remind you of the affirmation that you took at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me and understand me all right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When we stopped on Wednesday last week the last thing that we were talking about was Ajet Gashi. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, what happened after you learned that this Serb woman had been detained in Fustica in July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't say that she was Serb. She pretended she was handicapped. She tried to speak a little Albanian and she had a few things in her baggage which only people have mental disabilities could carry. I gave her a lift in my car from Fustica village to Lapusnik. She introduced herself as a Muslim woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why was she stopped in Fustica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had passed from one stronghold of KLA to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So was she suspected of something?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was suspected of being a spy, of trying to find out where the positions of KLA were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why did you bring her to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was arrested when I gave her the lift. And I was going to Lapusnik so I had to do the same journey. In order for her not to wait to be taken by another car, I took her in my car. She was tied up in her hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you arrived to Lapusnik, where did you bring her?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I brought her to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where -- where in the prison did you bring her, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once you enter the yard there is a door to a cellars and the right side. But it was built. It was not a cellar, actually. It was a living-room. In the corridor of that room I took her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, with the assist of the usher I'm going to show you U008-3669 the from Prosecution Exhibit P6. It's on page 4. Witness, can you look at that photograph, please? Is that the place where you brought this woman from Fustica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, to this place here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness has pointed to the door that is to the left of the light blue balustrade, what appears to be the main door on the -- on the ground floor of the building. That photograph can be taken away, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, what brought her after you brought her to that building?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took away -- they searched her bag and saw that she didn't carry any identity card. She had some threads. Nothing much to speak of. It was impossible to talk with her. She pretended to be a fool and then I left her there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you left her, did you question her?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But she didn't accept anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was your purpose in questioning her?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that she would admit something and that she wouldn't pretend to be a disabled person. But she kept playing that role. It was impossible to extract something from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you mistreat her in any way while questioning her?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Maybe I used a harsh tone or a loud voice, but I didn't mistreat her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you question her once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that one time that you questioned her, did you strike her on her body in any way?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No, I threatened her that if I'm going to ask her for the second time, I will beat her. But I didn't then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that "they searched her." Who searched her?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, I searched her. I searched her bag. And besides the guard, there wasn't anybody around that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who was the guard?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you see Shala there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the entrance of the yard I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was he with you when you questioned this woman?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did he do anything while you were questioning the woman?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did your questioning last, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 minutes or so, half an hour. Until I, as I said, searched her bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did something happen with this woman later?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the next day, in the evening, I am not very sure whether it was the next day or the day after, but it was in the evening at about 11.00. Qerqiz called me and told me to release the woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did he call you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] met him. I said I met him. He came and I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember where. It was near the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Lapusnik. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he tell you why she was to be released?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He just told me, Get rid of this stupid woman. Release her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went and took her with a car and drove her up to the position number 2, near that position. I tied her to an oak tree, to inform the guards not to fire at us, until we approached. I explained to them who we were. When I returned from the guard, she tried to be more coherent in her speech. Probably she must have thought that I was going to kill her because of what I had previously threatened her. She said that, I work as a maid in a clinic of the SUP I think or I work at the SUP, something like this. I'm not clear -- sure what she said. She also told me her name. So I let her up -- I accompanied her up to the asphalt road. I showed her the direction to Komorane. I told her to stick to the asphalt road and she went. When she approached some 150 metres to the Serb forces in Komorane I saw that she had some matches with her and she started to light the matches. And I didn't see any more of her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say that you first went to inform the guards not to fire at us, which guards are you speaking of?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the guards that protected the positions at night. Because we always kept guard at the positions, day in and day out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So just to be clear, you're talking about KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, was there a doctor in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did he work?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small room, or two small rooms one after another in the same yard where the staff was and they were used like a makeshift clinic. There was a small shelf with medicaments and there was a nurse as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall the doctor's name?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Zeqe Gashi. But his name could be longer. Zeqir. It was Dr. Zeqe Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, to your knowledge, did he treat soldiers in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how about civilians. Do you know if he treated civilians?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there were few civilians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to move to another topic. Did you ever see any Serbs at the prison?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in the end of June, in the second half of June. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the prison courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was young, a young man, maybe less than 18 years old, 16, 17. The other was a tall man in his 40s. Maybe he was 45. I spoke with them. I spoke with the son. They said that they came from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said you spoke with the son. Were these two father and son?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a young man. But I don't remember now. He said that it was a son. The father, he was worried about the young man. It was a very brief time that we met and they were completely free.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you mean "they were completely free"?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't look like in persons in prison. They didn't look arrested or imprisoned. They could behave freely, they had cigarettes, they could walk along the yard. They could talk to the soldiers, and later on I heard that both of them were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you -- you said you saw them two times. Can you describe more specifically where you saw them on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I've seen the young man in the yard. There is a well there, a drinking water well. And he was sitting there on the grass. And for the old man, I've seen him on the staircase. The staircase near the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that the staircase of the building that we have been talking about today?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was anybody with these two men, either time that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that they could speak with the guards. Did you see them speaking with guards?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They even played with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did they play?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could walk freely. They could play chess, but there was a chess game there. And I knew they were free to move about. They told me themselves, We are free.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, who -- who did they play chess with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could play chess with the guards. They could talk with the guard, with the soldiers. They could talk with whoever entered the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which guards did you see them -- if you can remember, which guards did you see them playing chess with or talking to?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point I'm going to object because I don't believe the witness has done anything other than speculate with regard to what could be done in terms of playing any games, chess or otherwise. I believe that Mr. Whiting is driving for an answer and is leading the witness into an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, there has been a statement by the witness. You can explore his foundation for that, but it should be his foundation, not yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How do you know they could play chess with the guards?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they -- that they were free to move about in the yard. The door to their room was open. Both of them didn't seem as if they were prisoners or detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, but please listen to me question. You said that they could play chess with the guards. And my question is: How did you know that.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the older man was sitting there was a chess game leaning Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. against the wall. Where he was sitting at the staircase I told you before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see him playing chess?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That day, Shala was not on guard when I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I believe you testified that you saw them talking to guards. Do you remember which guards they talked to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard who was on duty inside the prison, Murrizi and Shala. But I'm not sure whether it was Shala. I know that Murrizi too was there and that he too talked with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you testified that they -- these two men were released. Do you know how they were released?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that after a while, some -- Celiku came from Klecke and they took them somewhere and released them. But I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how do you know that, that Celiku came from Klecke and that they took them somewhere and released them. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the cars when they came. There were two jeeps. And I heard people say that these two Serbs are going to be released and that it was morning, whereas in the evening it was broadcast in the media that they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you said you saw two cars. Did you see Celiku?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw it only in the evening on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So did Celiku have anything to do, to your knowledge, with this release?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Celiku is the one who must have released them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why -- what is your basis for saying that. Why do you say that, that he must have been the one who released them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is what everybody said, that Celiku released them and because Celiku was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But to be clear, you did not see -- your testimony is that you did not see Celiku on the day that they were released?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said before, I didn't. But when I saw the interview broadcast in the evening that they were released, I saw the cars. But Celiku, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever see a Mercedes vehicle at or near the prison compound?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a Mercedes seen on the other side of the prison. Where we took the oath. They said it belongs to a Serb. To a Serb tradesman, but he too was released. The car was given back to him and he was allowed to go. I don't when, but I know that he was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The car was there for several days. And I know that when they allowed him to go, they gave him the car back and that he was -- he left in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But me question, Witness, is How do you know this. Did you see it, were you told, how do you know this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard people say that. I didn't see him when he was released. I saw the car, however, when it was staying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember who told you this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody spoke about such things. It was not a secret. Everybody knew that he was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to move to a new topic. Do you know man by the name of Hasan Hoxha or Hasan Dobreva?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to ask show you a photograph U003-8697, and for the record the name is blocked out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is Hasan Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That can be taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know him as Hasan Hoxha or Hasan Dobreva?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by both names. But he was more known as Hasan Dobreva.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know him before you -- your time in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the high school, from 1973 I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see him at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the accurate time. But it was the end of July or the beginning -- end of June, sorry, and beginning of July. Maybe end of June is more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road that goes from the kitchen to the prison. In the place when you turn right, there was a guard there. Often members of the territorial units stayed on guard there. It was a small lawn where they brought him. There I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, when you turn right coming out of the kitchen or turn right coming out of the prison?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you leave the kitchen, and take the road that goes to the prison, you take a left, then go uphill. Berisa -- maybe about 200 metres the road turns to the left, to that -- at that corner there was a lawn and this is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how was it that you saw him? What was happening?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They brought him there. They had arrested him somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: didn't know that he was arrested or detained when they had brought him there. In the meantime others came. Ymer came. He talked with him. He told him something like, I have heard that nobody could throw you down and before Hasan could reply it him he gave him a blow and he fell on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who brought him to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shala's soldier from Sedlare.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which Shala are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the soldiers of Sedlare, Shale village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did you know that. How did you know that the soldiers from Sedlare/Shale brought him to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with Hasan there. Afterwards, I learned how he came to Sedlare.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he had come to join the KLA or to assist the KLA. That was his initial goal. After these -- we exchange as few words only until the incident I described with Ymer occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, the translation that we got was that I, meaning you, didn't know that he was arrested or detained when they brought him there. Was it you or he didn't know that he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither myself nor he knew that he arrested [as interpreted]. He was smoking some Dunhill cigarettes. He gave us cigarettes. And I don't believe that he knew that he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from Ymer, do you remember any other soldiers that were around him when you were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zenel came along with Ymer. There were also others, members from the territorial units. But I don't remember there were seven or eight people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember where on -- on Hasan's body Ymer struck him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He struck him on the head, on the front part of the head. In the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know why he Hasan was arrested?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards, I heard that he was arrested. I didn't know then. But in August I heard how he was arrested, how he was brought there and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear a reason why he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken on the allegation that he was a collaborator of Serbia as a spy, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is that something that you heard in August?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it after he was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how you heard that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever was arrested was done so on reasons of being a spy. Everybody who was in that prison was accused of being a collaborator or a spy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you saw him on that day, did you see him again in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I heard that he was badly beaten, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you hear that he was badly beaten?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know from who in particular, but I heard that from soldiers. That he was badly beaten. I don't know whether he admitted being a spy or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear what happened to him later?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I asked somebody in July and that he told me that he was done short work of, by means -- by that I understood that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you later see some bodies near the village of Morina?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it before or after you had seen Hasan Hoxha?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 10 or 15 days after I met Hasan Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many bodies did you see?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three, in one place. Two in one place and three in another place. But I didn't come out of my car to see who there were because there was a strong wind. No, it was a strong smell, a stench. It was very hot. But I talked with someone -- a shepherd who was taking care of his cattle or sheep there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did the shepherd say?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked him, Who are they? And he said -- I told him, Why aren't you burying them because it smells so bad. Why don't you bury them. As if joke -- as if joking he told me, You bring the bodies here and you expect us to take care of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Had you brought the bodies there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me. He meant -- he meant us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "Us" being what?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you think there was any connection between these bodies and Hasan Hoxha?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't come out of the car to identify them because there was a steep path, and my handbrake was not working. I wanted to go out and see whether it was Hasan; I didn't. But I thought that probably one of them must be Hasan Hoxha. That was my personal belief then. Nobody told me anything, that it was him. With the exception of what I had heard, that I mentioned earlier, that he was done short work of. That's why I thought that maybe he was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will adjourn now. We will resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you know somebody by the same of Vesel from Godance?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about him, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about him while you were at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he had been arrested. I don't know where he was taken to. I never saw him. But I know that people spoke of him. He was a well-known person. He was seen on TV publicly when someone from Belgrade would come to discuss with Rugova and he would go there in the capacity of an Albanian representative. He was saying that he was representing Albanians according to the votes, but to my opinion, these votes were manipulated. I know -- I've heard that this person was going out with some Serbs and Romas. He was in these negotiations or discussions more than nine times in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are these things that you have told us about this person the reasons that he was arrested, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There couldn't be any other reason. Such people with the help of the then Serb government, they would use the names of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Albanians who had the right to vote. They will collect 5.000, 6.000 votes and then they will appoint someone to speak in the name of the Albanians and bring decisions in their name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if he was in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I heard that he was arrested and that he was brought to Lapusnik, but I never saw him. This is only speculation or words amongst soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever speak with Zenel or Timi about the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you describe the conversations. What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Other soldiers would speak as well, how someone was taken in and how he was interrogated and how he was maltreated. Nothing concrete in name and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But specifically would Zenel and Timi talk about these things?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And specifically do you remember what they would say, what they talked about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For the moment I can't remember. There were several discussions. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did either of them ever talk about karate?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zenel said he was a karate, that he exercised this art and that he did that in the French league. He spoke something like this, but personally I didn't have the impression that that was the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you not have the impression that that was the truth?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could clearly see that Zenel could not handle a weapon. If he was a well trained -- in the French league he would have learned more about weapons. As for karate, I know that he knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever see either of those men with a mask?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe yes. Not Timi. But as for Zenel, I believe yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember where you saw him with a mask?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it before that on one occasion when Qerqiz, Zenel and someone else came out from the prison, I said that two of them were wearing masks. One of them was Zenel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to move to a different topic. During the time that you were in Lapusnik, in the end of May, June, and July of 1998, did you go to any other villages?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I have had many journeys. In reference to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's not in reference to anything specific; it's just a question if you went to any other villages during the time that you were in Lapusnik. Or did you stay in Lapusnik the entire time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there was fighting, I would go to Kroimire as assistance with the unit. Specifically I went to Blinaje on one occasion, following Qerqiz's order. And once with two other persons I went to Carralluke village but not with the order of Qerqiz. I received the order from the two persons who came with me. They said, We have an order, but didn't specify who gave them the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Klecke?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever go to any other villages that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this moment I can't remember. I've been to Malisevo, Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that you went to Kroimire assisting with the unit when there was fighting. Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in June. I don't know exactly when. Maybe in end of June. But there was fighting in Carraleve gorge, in Zborce. It was end of June or beginning of July, around this time. I don't remember exactly, but five or six of us went.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how you knew that there was fighting in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As for the fighting up to Kroimire and when Kroimire was in fighting, you could hear the firing even in Lapusnik because they were not only shelling the KLA positions but also the civilian population. They were shelling villages as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who -- was there a commander in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the beginning it was Ramiz Qeriqi, Luani.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now you also said that you went to Blinaje. Was there a commander in Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes when Blinaje was taken and until the end the commander was Shukri Buja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when was Blinaje taken, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blinaje was taken in June. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a commander above Ramiz Qeriqi and Shukri Buja?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for that territory there wasn't another commander. It was from Celiku downwards. Celiku was the commander while the others were lower ranking commanders, Shukri and Ramiz.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know a soldier by the name of Avni Sinani?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see him in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there 15 or 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he came in the beginning of June. He was admitted in the ranks or sometime he kept the order during lineup because he was an officer, a former JNA officer. And after that I know that he went it Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did he go to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date, but for 10 or 15 days he was in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How do you know he went to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When -- do you remember when you saw him in Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when in June?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure but after the 15th of June. Around 15th or 20th of June I saw him in Blinaje. It was in the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see him at all after that date?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for another time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in Blinaje. There was a fighting there on that day, and I saw him for the second time on that day. There was an attack launched by the Serb forces against the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the date. I don't remember the date. However, it was the first attack that the Serb forces launched on Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Other than the two occasions when you saw him in Blinaje, do you know where he was after he left Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I think he was in Blinaje. And where he left after Blinaje, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, with the assistance of the usher I'm going show you a diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's at tab 15 and it's also going to be put on Sanction with the assistance of -- if we could switch to Sanction, please. And on the Sanction the signature on the bottom has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a question that you asked earlier. And I made that drawing fast. It is an approximate drawing. You can see the Crnoljevo road to Prizren and the Peja-Pristina road. In the middle there is Klecka. And the other places that are marked fall in a territory that was under Klecka's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, at Klecka there is a Q inside the circle. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Q refers to Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the Pristina-Prizren road is at the top of the page; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: At Blinaje there is circle and it has SH and a dot and then B. Can you tell us what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sh is the "sh" sound in Albanian and refers to Shukri Buja who was the commander in Blinaje. In Kroimire the name of Luan is circled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is the name that is next to Luznica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Kumanova. Commander Kumanova was in Luznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you have arrows from -- going towards Klecka from Blinaje, Kroimire, Luznica, Javor, Lladrovc, Malisheve, Terpeze, Novoselle, and Lapusnik. Just to be clear, what do those arrows pointing at Klecka mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this is approximately the territory that was under Klecke's command. Fustica, Lapusnik, Nekovce, Bajice, Lladrovc, Luznica, Blinaje, Kroimire. These villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now at Lapusnik you have a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with an arrows pointing towards Qerqizi. Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the positions in Lapusnik there. There Were five positions in Lapusnik, with the exception of one position in Kishna Reka which was not under Klecka's command. And another unit in Orlate was also not under Klecka's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On that point you have an arrow from Kishna Reka which goes -- which crosses the Peja-Pristina road and has "Plumov," [sic] and then an arrow from Arlat that also crosses the road that says "Pellumbi." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the Pellumbi units. Not Plumbi, but Pellumbi units. And they were on the opposite of Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Above the word Qerqizi there is a Q3. Can you tell us what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Celiku 3. The unit in Lapusnik was called so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And finally at the bottom of the page there's a date and a signature. Is that date the date that you drew it, you drew this diagram?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, I didn't make this drawing for here but it was for the moment because we repeated things many times. And that's why I draw this and included this territory to explain how approximately it was. And this is how approximately it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this diagram be given a number and I would propose that rather than putting it under seal that the signature simply be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received the signature to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, with the assistance of the usher, I'm going to show you Prosecution Exhibit 135.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if it could be placed on the ELMO, please. Actually if you could place the back of the photograph on the ELMO. It's the second page. You have the second page there. That's the back. And if that could be placed on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise any of these names, either the names or the pseudonyms?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see any of these people in Lapusnik while you were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be given a pen and if you could just circle the names that you remember seeing in Lapusnik during those months in the summer of 1998 that you were there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. You've put a mark -- you've circled number, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19 and 20. You've put a mark next to number five. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was circled by mistake. Because your question was who was in Lapusnik. This person was not in Lapusnik, and he joined later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you put an arrow next to number 18. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a soldier in Lapusnik. But in Nekovce, while number 20, this person is an inhabitant of Lapusnik but wasn't a soldier there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how about number 21? You did not circle number 21. Do you know anything about that person?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him by name. I know him, but not very well. I can't remember him according to his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this could be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And we're done with that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, in July of 1998 did you have occasion to go to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I wasn't there during the first day of fighting. On the second day, I'm not sure it was 18 or 19, the day, of July. I think that on the 19th of July I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who did you go with, if anybody?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went by car. We were five persons. With another car there were two or three other persons following us. With the car we went there --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just going to interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, how did you get from Lapusnik to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went by car up to Malisevo. From Malisevo to Dragobilje village, again we went by car. In the evening we got together on a hill above Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you get from Lapusnik to Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said we went by car. We had an Opel Record, a green one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I meant what read did you take.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the road from Arlat, from Arlat we took left from Malisevo. From Malisevo we went to Orahovac. You drive through the centre of the town, and then drive along the hill above the Dragobilje. When night came, as I said, we got together on that hill above Orahovac through the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the KLA control the road that you took from Lapusnik to Malisevo to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Up to the vicinity of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how long it took you to drive from Lapusnik up to the vicinity of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you drive without stopping anywhere it doesn't take long. But we stopped at Dragobilje, at Malisevo for a while and then at Dragobilje we stayed for a long while. For about -- this trip took us about three Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hours, even more than three hours, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you drive without stopping, how long does it take?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it lasts 40 or 50 minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think you maybe partially answered this question, but why did you go to Orahovac at this time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting in Orahovac, major fightings those days. Serb forces had attacked and even though our unit our units had been defeated and had withdrawn and the Serb forces were committing massacres against the civilian population. We heard rumours that about 500 civilians were killed and most of them were killed. I can't tell you for sure whether it was 500 or more, but around that figure. So we went there to withdraw those people that could be withdrawn from Orahovac to take them to the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you say in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, that night and up to the next morning. Without -- when the morning was not yet on, we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met some citizens who came there who had fled and they told us that there are no more civilians, only Serb forces in Orahovac and they proved us that they were the last to leave the place. One of them was the a member of the KLA who had gone there to pull out his family and he assured us there was nobody there. That's why we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you returned where did you go?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you go by yourself or with others back to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with the others. Again we returned by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, while you were away from Lapusnik, did you see any prisoners that had been taken from Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day that the Lapusnik gorge fell, in the morning, I don't know whether it was 10.00 or 11.00. It was around that time. I think that on that day, when we went to the road that leads to Novoselle I saw a stopped or parked bus at --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the time when you were in Malisevo. During the time that you went to Orahovac you went through Malisevo. In Malisevo, did you see any prisoners that had been taken from Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went close to the door and we saw some prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Close to what door?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an unfinished building close by. The headquarters in Malisevo. In the cellar of that building, I mean. Or better to say on the ground floor, not in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you describe how it -- how it happened that you went close to the door and saw prisoners there. How did that come to happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone told us that there are some prisoners. And we went to see. Someone who was on guard there at the door. And two or three of us, or four of us, I think, went there to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were they men, were they women, were they both?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were men and women. But mostly men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you tell if they were Serbs or Albanians?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rumours that they are Serbs. But in Orahovac, there are also Albanians who speak Serbian. Most of the people there, in Orahovac even though they are Albanians, they speak a language similar to Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to move to a new topic. Do you remember anything about journalists, some journalists being stopped at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some journalists who were stopped. Usually we used to stop the journalists when they wanted to enter the territory controlled by KLA. I remember several cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember one case that involved Russian journalists?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you remember about it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they were stopped at a crossroads. They were asked where they were coming from, who they were. I know that Qerqiz was not there. I know that they were held for one or two hours waiting to contact someone. There was also an interpreter with them, an Albanian interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You say that Qerqiz was not there. What do you mean he was not there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not there at this time. Two soldiers were missing. They were -- they were -- they remained in Orahovac and every day Ymer and Qerqiz went to look for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did this event with the Russian journalists occur before or after you went to Orahovac yourself, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was after we went to Orahovac. Because neither Ymer nor Qerqiz were in Orahovac during those days. They were not regularly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were not regularly in Orahovac or not regularly in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that on -- when the journalists, the Russian journalists were stopped, Ymer and Qerqiz were not in Lapusnik at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, going back to what happened with the journalists, do you remember -- do you know where they were stopped?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were they stopped?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were stopped at position number 1, in the asphalt road. There was the guard there at the asphalt road where they stopped them. There were also soldiers from the opposite side of the road were also on guard and they were asked, as I said, where they were coming from and where they were there. But the fact that they spoke Russian made them suspects for the eyes of the KLA soldiers. Because they thought they might be Serbs and they posed as Russians. In fact, this is what I think even now, that they were Serbs disguised as Russians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, how do you know this? How do you know this happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because they asked for -- through radio use, they called for Qerqiz. The radio was near where I was, and so they tried to contact Qerqiz for two hours, but they couldn't find him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many radios were in Lapusnik at this time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was sure. But there was another one. I'm not sure whether it was in regular use, but one was in constant use. The second one might be with Qerqiz or with the headquarters. But I believe there were two small ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said that the radio was near where you were. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the position. The radio was with me. It was not near but it was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see the journalists yourself?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe that, please.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there, the soldiers had stopped them and they were keeping them outside of the asphalt road in a certain lawn that was there. They tried hard to find out whether they were Serbs or not. And until some others came and fetched them, they were kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened. What did you see?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there was no one to ask, Pellumbi unit and the soldiers who were in Orlate from the military police where there on duty, they came. With a car and someone from Pellumbi unit came and they picked them up and took them to their headquarters then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many journalists did you see, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were three, four together with the interpreter. There might have been two. But 90 per cent, I think they were three.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The interpreter introduced himself as a Russian professor. But regarding those journalists, I think they were released because I saw three when they were coming back and I know that they were released on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When they were on -- on the road before the Pellumbi unit came, did anything happen to them, the journalists or the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone gave them some slaps but not many. But they beat the professor more because they suspected that he might be a Serb mixed up with them. Even though he had proper papers to prove the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see the interpreter beaten?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember who beat him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers who were there, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time has passed. I know that they have beaten him. The soldiers who were there on the road. Both the soldiers from our unit and from the other unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that they were picked up by the Pellumbi unit and taken to their headquarters. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because I saw the van when it came and picked all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But how do you know they went to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because from there it was easy to communicate with Guri 3 unit. And we could hear when the unit -- Pellumbi unit came and took them to their own headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that by radio you could hear that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the radio. But I also saw them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said that the journalists were later released and that you -- you saw them coming back. Can you describe that, please?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon. I don't remember what time. It might be 4.00, I don't know. We saw three people walking along the asphalt road towards Komorane. And we asked who were they, thinking that they might be some Albanian civilians walking that way. And they were told that they are those Russian journalists who were detained earlier and now they are released. And they were walking back on foot along this asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the position, and during all of the time they were within view, I -- I looked at them through the binoculars. It was very hot and I couldn't have full view of them but I saw them part of the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you say you were in the position, is that position 2?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the interpreter that was with them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that he was detained, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he did not return with them and there were rumours that he was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to Qerqiz about this incident?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I met him, late that night. I believe it was that night, late. It was not on the next day. I wanted to report to him what happened, and he told me that, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere in the main road that leads to the headquarters in Lapusnik. Near the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was he alone or was he with anybody?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with Ymer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you say and what did he say?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that, I'd like to inform you about what happened today and he told me that, We have been already informed so we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that I believe it was that night, late and then you said it was not on the next day. Can you be more clear about your memory of when you told this to Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm more certain that it was that same night. But it might be also on the next day. But not during the day, at night. But I believe more that it was on the same night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is it possible that it was any other night or -- or is it either that night or the next night?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was either that night or the next night. But not further than that. But I am more certain, I think, that it was the first night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you what's been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 129. If you could -- it's hard to see much on the cover. If you could just flip through this document, just look at the pages of the document.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that even before. It locks similar to the notebook we used to keep notes in the positions in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you look at the -- in some -- on some of the pages there are some pseudonyms.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For example, Skifteri, Uka, Graniti, Minatori?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't know who Skifteri was. But Cubi, Graniti, these, yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How do you know those names?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were soldiers at position number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How about Motori. Do you recognise that name?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes he was also in position 1. Uka too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Rambo?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes Rambo too was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, please, turn -- maybe the usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: To turn to U0023486 and it's -- on the English translation for those who have it, it's page 33. If we could switch to the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you see there's an entry on that page for the 20th of July, 1998 at 10.20 and it says: "A car arrives from Russian Central Television. Translator Shaban Hoti." And then gives some information about this person. And then -- and then it lists some names, "Galanov Aleksander, Mamaev Viktor, Safiu Ulin," and then a licence plate.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of that information in relation to the story about the Russian journalists that you told us?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very similar, with the exception that I don't recall this car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That can be taken away, thank you. Your Honour, I think that is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, from the time -- from the day that you returned from Orahovac until the day you left Lapusnik, how often did you see Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you be more specific.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, when we went to fighting in Fustica, and once or two other times after that. So in total two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How about before you went -- well, you've already told us that you saw him when you told him about the Russian journalists. Did you see him any other times before you went to the fighting in Fustica?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. But I believe I have met him during the evenings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know -- when you say you met him during the evenings, is that every evening or some of the evenings or one of the evenings?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some of the evenings, not every evening. Two or three times altogether, after what I mentioned with respect to the Russian journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And are those two or three times before or after you went to Fustica, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before and after. The most important thing that I remember, it was in the night of the 25th of July when I met him. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know -- when you did not see him in Lapusnik, do you know where he was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he was in Lapusnik. But I know that they went very regularly, I would say, to look for those two soldiers who had remained in Orahovac. They did so especially in the afternoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who would go look for those soldiers aside from Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was Ymer, and maybe someone from the soldiers could go. One or two others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what's the longest amount of time do you think they went away from Lapusnik to look for those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to look and -- go there and look for someone, it would take you three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But do you think that is the longest amount of time that they would leave Lapusnik it look for the soldiers or would they at times leave for longer periods of time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they left for a longer period. Usually they were away for an afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, during this time period, this last week that you were in Lapusnik, did you receive an order regarding the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this happened during the first day of the fighting in Orahovac. That day there was shelling also in Lapusnik for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So was this before or after you yourself went to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until I was in the position. The -- Mesuesi came and he invited me to go with him. It was afternoon. He was worried. On the way he told me what it was all about. I just could see that he was upset. First maybe I thought this was an act of provocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What -- what position were you in?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In position number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that he told you what it was all about on the way. What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that, We have orders to go and kill those who are in the prison downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened -- so what happened next?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there but on the way we talked about what he wanted to tell me. He said that there is nobody there, Qerqizi or Ymer were not there. Nobody was there. He said that he was afraid that the war was raging in Orahovac and shelling -- there was a lot of shelling also where we were, and he was afraid, afraid of Serb forces penetrating into our positions. So when he told me about that, I tried to convince him that no danger could come to us aside from distant shelling. After we went to the yard, there he decided to turn back, and we didn't go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which yard did you get to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the yard of the prison, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he tell you who gave him the orders to kill those in the prison?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't mention any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you do after you decided not to go inside?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was convinced that no threat was facing us, he as I said earlier seemed upset, so we left it, we didn't go inside. So we didn't mention this anymore after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to move to the topic of the attack of -- of the Serbs on Lapusnik on the 25th and 26th of July. Where were you when this happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning the guard warned us of movements of the enemy. When the light became greater, we could see large concentration of forces coming from Komorane. At Komorane checkpoint we saw two convoys of armoured cars, tanks and APCs as far as the eye could see. They were coming in the direction of Pristina. At 5.20 they started the attack. They took positions, some on the right and some on the left, and they started to fire at the positions of the KLA in that territory all at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was that on the 25th or the 26th, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th I said. This I had not forget. It was morning of the 25th of July, 5.20 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did the fighting continue that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They went on until late at night. Till 10.00, 11.00 in the evening. But we could hear some sporadic shots even during the night, until they took positions very close to our positions, maybe 200 or 300 metres from our positions. In the morning they started again, to fire against us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you leave Lapusnik at some point?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how you left Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left without any specific orders. We felt a great threat. Not only the Serb forces were very close to us. They had entered Lapusnik. So I thought that under these circumstances I could withdraw, and I did withdraw. I went up to the hill that leads to Berisa to the Vojvoda neighbourhood. Some people helped me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you -- on your way out of Lapusnik, did you pass by the prison compound?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The doors of the prison were open.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you see anything inside?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No sound could be heard. I didn't go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Berisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Berisa?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until I drank some water and went on with my journey to Novoselle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you arrive in Novoselle on the same day, on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I needed a doctor's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did you hear anything about what happened to the prisoners from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day. Someone said that they were released and they had left before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear anything on later days?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After two days, I heard rumours that two or three of them had agreed to help in the fighting and one of them had gone with Ymer to carry shells and the cannon in the course of which he was injured, when Ymer was killed. He was injured on the arm. On the 28th, I met Qerqiz. He gave me a lift with his car to Klecke and he said that he had given each of them a piece of paper, a document and all of them were released. I asked him because the family members were asking for them and he told me that, They are free now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: He gave you a lift to Klecke from where on the 28th?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in between Terpeze and Novoselle villages, on the way to Novoselle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said you heard rumours about it or three of the prisoners helping in the fighting. Can you tell us how you heard those rumours?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One who had expressed his wish to help, he had been with Ymer when he got killed and that he himself had been injured in the arm. And he had carried Ymer on his own shoulder up to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you talk to this person yourself?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
